# `@elabs-ai/components-terminal`

> Terminal surfaces: shell/agent output and coding-agent CLI look-alikes.

Part of **brand-ui**, a source-owned, token-driven React component system.
Published to the **public npm registry** under the `@elabs-ai` scope — it
installs like any other npm dependency, with no registry configuration and
no token required. See `docs/CONSUMING.md`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @elabs-ai/components-tokens @elabs-ai/components-terminal
pnpm add @xterm/addon-fit@"^0.11.0"  # optional peer
pnpm add @xterm/xterm@"^6.0.0"  # optional peer
```

## Set up styling (do not skip)

Components are Tailwind v4 classes backed by semantic tokens. Two lines in
your CSS entry, or **everything renders unstyled** — the single most common
mistake:

```css
@import "@elabs-ai/components-tokens/styles.css";
@source "../node_modules/@elabs-ai/components-terminal/dist";
```

The `@source` line is required because Tailwind ignores `node_modules`. Add
one per brand-ui package you render. Then wrap your app once:

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "@elabs-ai/components-tokens";

<ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">{children}</ThemeProvider>;
```

## What's in it

31 exported components — including `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_GUTTER`, `InteractiveTerminal`, `Terminal`, `TERMINAL_TOOL_CALL_STATUSES`, `TERMINAL_TRANSCRIPT_ROW_KINDS`.

Don't guess the API — ask the CLI:

```bash
pnpm add -D @elabs-ai/components-cli
pnpm exec brand-ui search <query>   # find a component
pnpm exec brand-ui docs <Name>      # its real props, from source
```

## Using an AI coding agent?

For Claude Code, install the plugin from this repo's checkout:

```
/plugin marketplace add .
/plugin install brand-ui
```

`brand-ui docs <Name>` returns intent, composition, state→token mappings and
anti-patterns — tell your agent to run it instead of guessing a prop. The CLI
also runs as an MCP server (`brand-ui mcp`).

Tailwind and Next.js wiring, per-package extras, agent enablement and a
prompt for migrating an existing project: `docs/CONSUMING.md`.

## Status — registered, deliberately empty

This package is **scaffolded and fully registered, but ships no components yet**
(issue #114). The barrel is empty on purpose:

- **#116** moves `Terminal` and `InteractiveTerminal` here from
  `@elabs-ai/components-ai`, together with the optional `@xterm/*` peers and the
  `ansi-to-react` dependency.
- **#117** adds the coding-agent CLI look-alikes, which is also when the ANSI
  token group from **#115** is consumed.

Until #116 lands there is nothing to import, so the package is not yet wired
into `fixtures/consumer-smoke`.

## Where it sits in the dependency graph

`@elabs-ai/components-terminal` is a **layer-2 leaf**:
`tokens` → `ui`/`icons` → `terminal`. It may depend on
`@elabs-ai/components-tokens`, `-icons` and `-ui`, and **nothing may depend on
it**. In particular `@elabs-ai/components-ai` must never import it — that is a
sideways edge and `pnpm dep-direction:check` fails on it. A chat transcript that
wants to show a terminal receives one as `children`.

A terminal emulator's optional peers exist to reproduce a shell, not to render a
`UIMessage`; keeping them out of `@elabs-ai/components-ai` is what keeps that
package cheap to install. See
`docs/decisions/2026-09-01-brainless-adoption-architecture.md` § 1.
